title: Superbot-induced gap closure is local and restores native tissue density

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Superbot-induced gap closure is local and restores native tissue density

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Neuronal gap closure occurs only at the site where a superbot is placed; the neuronal coverage density there is statistically indistinguishable from intact tissue outside the scratch, while adjacent and distant parts of the scratch have significantly lower coverage.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Gumuskaya G 2024, Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells › Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Thus, the density of the induced gap closure area that formed as a result of the presence of the superbot represented full (statistically indistinguishable from 100%) recovery of the original tissue and was uniquely different from the surrounding scratch area.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Gumuskaya G, Srivastava P, Cooper BG, Lesser H, Semegran B, Garnier S, Levin M, “Motile Living Biobots Self-Construct from Adult Human Somatic Progenitor Seed Cells”, Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany) (2024), doi:10.1002/advs.202303575; section “Results › Anthrobots Can Promote Gap Closures on Scratched Live Neuronal Monolayer Tissues”. Scope: Superbots on scratched hiNSC-derived human neuronal monolayers; bridges maintained over 3 days (5 of 10)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-anthrobots-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Spatial density comparisons are directly reproducible in principle. The public five-bridge analysis supports localization, but its statistical framing cannot establish restored equivalence without margins and adequate power.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Recalculate binarized neuron-pixel density at closure, intact, adjacent, and distal regions and test localization and equivalence to intact density rather than relying only on nonsignificance.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nonsignificance at p=0.37 does not prove equivalence to 100% recovery.

Manual threshold and region selection can affect pixel density.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.36
analysis feasibility: 0.86
data existence: 0.64
discriminating power: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.98

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Local coverage versus adjacent scratch and versus intact tissue is a defined density contrast. The paper reports full recovery under the bridge and lower coverage elsewhere, without depositing the region measurements. Manual thresholding makes the equality claim sensitive to choices that cannot be repeated from the summary alone.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Binarize neuronal coverage under the bridge, in adjacent scratch, in distant scratch and in intact monolayer, and test equality with intact tissue and inequality with the rest of the scratch. Coverage under the bridge statistically matching intact tissue, and only there, would support full local recovery; a deficit under the bridge, or equal filling along the scratch, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The comparison uses the bridges that remained in place for three days.

Pixel densities after manual thresholding are not in a public table.

Statistical indistinguishability from 100% recovery depends on sample size and on the threshold.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.16
discriminating power: 0.46
analysis feasibility: 0.18
data existence: 0.18
operationalizability: 0.9
